title: Diversity gaps in human aging research
bottleneck: Aging biomarkers, genetic studies, and clinical trials overwhelmingly sample people of European ancestry, yet aging trajectories differ across populations due to genetics, environment, and lifetime exposures. The 2025 open-problems roadmap in GeroScience flagged diversity in human aging as severely underrepresented.
why_it_blocks: Interventions validated in one population may fail or harm in others, and the global majority ages without relevant data. The longevity field risks building precision aging medicine for a narrow slice of humanity.
current_state: Biobanks are slowly diversifying; epigenetic clocks are being recalibrated across ancestries. But most geroscience trials still recruit homogeneous cohorts, and environmental-exposure research is only 2% of open problems. All-of-Us and similar diverse biobanks are beginning to fill the gap, but geroscience trials still recruit predominantly European-ancestry cohorts, limiting generalizability of aging biomarkers.
